 Order
 % 03.12.2025
 Crl. M. (Bail) 448/2025
1.

The present appeal has been preferred by the appellant seeking quashing/setting aside of the impugned Judgment dated 27.02.2024 and Order on Sentence dated 30.03.2024, passed by learned Trial Court in Sessions Case No.527/2017 in FIR No. 213/2017, under Sections 367, 376, 377, 323 IPC and 06 POCSO Act, registered at Police Station Khyala, Delhi, whereby appellant has been held guilty and has been, inter alia, sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life.
2.
Vide this application, the appellant is seeking suspension of his sentence during pendency of present appeal.
3. Mr. Sunil Choudhary, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has already undergone substantial incarceration of around five years and his conduct in jail is satisfactory.
4. It is submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt against the appellant and there are contradictions in the statement of the witnesses.
It is further submitted that the family of the appellant This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/12/2025 at 21:38:50 consists of his mother and father.
His mother is suffering from slip disc, due to which she is unable to walk without support.

The appellant is handicapped and also suffers from Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).
5.
Learned APP for the State submits that the present case is of kidnapping and rape of minor girl aged around 9 years and at the time of incident, the accused/appellant was already HIV patient.
He submits that the prosecutrix had identified the appellant during the trial and she has been consistent in her statements and narrated the entire incident in detail in the Court.

It is submitted Mannu vs State Gnct Of Delhi on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182439611/
1 that the MLC of minor girl also affirms sexual assault.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the appellant has failed miserably to rebut the presumption under Section 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act.
6. We have perused the affidavit filed by the appellant which reveals that the appellant is implicated in two other cases of almost similar nature.
7. We have carefully considered the rival contentions and have perused the Trial Court Record (TCR).
Taking note of the testimony of the prosecution witness and the other material placed on record, we, at the moment, do not find any compelling reason to suspend the sentence.
8. Accordingly, the present application stands dismissed.
9. List in due course.
VIVEK CHAUDHARY, J MANOJ JAIN, J DECEMBER 3, 2025/r/nc
